subject.title: feat(googlechat): support Application Default Credentials for outbound auth

question: Should keyless Google Chat ADC be allowed to use `google-auth-library`'s Compute/gcp-metadata metadata-server path as-is, or must this PR add an OpenClaw-owned guard before merge?
rationale: Source and dependency inspection show the remaining risk is a real security-boundary/product decision, not a purely mechanical code defect: the desired GCE keyless path depends on direct metadata-server requests outside the existing Google Chat guarded transporter.

options.title: Require guarded metadata ADC
options.body: Require the PR to route or constrain Compute metadata token lookup through an OpenClaw-owned guard before merge, preserving the existing Google Chat auth hardening boundary.

options.title: Accept opt-in Compute ADC
options.body: Approve the direct metadata-server dependency path as an intentional opt-in exception for GCP-hosted Google Chat deployments, with docs/tests noting the runtime failure mode when ADC is unavailable.

options.title: Pause Chat ADC
options.body: Keep keyless Google Chat ADC out of core until a sponsored auth-boundary design decides how bundled channel ADC should handle metadata services.

recommendation.title: Require guarded metadata ADC
recommendation.body: Require the PR to route or constrain Compute metadata token lookup through an OpenClaw-owned guard before merge, preserving the existing Google Chat auth hardening boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest ownership signal is the prior merged Google Chat auth transport hardening and dependency-boundary work.
